blocks.text: Between 20 July and 19 November 2026 I used Claude Code as a working partner on 70 distinct SAP ABAP use cases across ONGC Videsh (47), PAL (6) and the Astral / Project UDAY engagement through KPMG (11), plus 6 reusable or not-yet-attributed items. The work covers complete applications (CDS / RAP dashboards, a credit-memo approval workflow, forecasting), new reports and interfaces, enhancements, S/4HANA remediation of 51 program includes, root-cause analysis of production issues, and the toolkit that makes the AI loop repeatable.

Estimated conventional effort for this work is **2,954 hours**; the AI-assisted effort, which counts every development hour available in the period, is **587 hours**. That is **2,367 hours (296 man-days) saved, a 80% weighted reduction**. Of this, 1,440 hours (180 man-days) sit on 26 use cases already confirmed in the system (activated, tested, deployed or confirmed by the user or client).

items: Every use case traces to a repository folder, its issue log and its commits. Nothing is counted without that trail.

Baselines are estimates from a stated rubric. Actual effort comes from commit timestamps and is scaled so that it adds up to all development time available in the period. That deliberately overstates the AI-assisted side.
Sensitivity: if conventional baselines were 30% lower, savings would be 1,481 hours (185 man-days, 72%); if 50% lower, 890 hours (111 man-days, 60%).
Tier B items (32) are delivered but have no activation or test result in the logs yet. ATC corrections are not yet imported or re-run in ATC, and are not presented as closed findings.
T&G: no document, log or commit in the repository names this project. The Astral (UDAY) engagement is reported separately and can be re-mapped in one cell of the register.

The filed client timesheets (August and September 2026), used for the admin share and dated pre-repository activity only.
No document, issue log, commit or timesheet in the repository names a project 'T&G'.
Client timesheets record hours per client per day, not per object; they were not used as per-object effort actuals.
No conventional (manual) effort baselines exist in project records; baselines are rubric estimates by work type and complexity.
ATC: no import, activation, syntax check or ATC re-run of the 51 corrected includes is recorded; the 847-finding figure comes from the work log, not from an export in the repository.
20/07 - 18/08/26 has dated narrative records only (handoff, work log, timesheet text) - no timestamps; 17-19/08 have no record.
AI token / cost consumption is not stored in the repository.
No billing or day rates are recorded, so no monetary value is computed.
32 delivered use cases have no recorded activation / test result (tier B); each confirmation moves it to tier A.
Four AI-era deliveries have no session or time record and are listed but not quantified.
Mail threads, meetings, SAP-side debugging and testing that produced no commit are not visible in the repository.
**Effort without AI** = rubric hours for the work type and complexity x scope factor. The ATC row instead uses the correction blocks actually applied (section 8).

**Actual effort with AI** = MAX(minimum-effort floor, git session hours x 1.68 + dated pre-repository hours) + any rework allowance. The factor is set so that the hours allocated across all use cases equal the 436 development hours available in the period (63 working days x 8 h, less the 13.5% admin share from the filed timesheet).
**Saved** = without - with; **reduction** = saved / without; **man-days** = saved / 8; **productivity improvement** = without / with - 1.
Project totals are weighted (summed hours), never an average of row percentages. Recurring automation savings are kept separate.

items: **Root cause before code.** ZMM_TMS_STATUS: a blank Excel export traced to no_out = '0' on all 44 field-catalog entries - one constant changed, confirmed on DEV the same day (28/10/26). blocks.caption: Case study at a glance
rows: Project / object
ONGC Videsh (OVL) - ZFI_JIB_STATUS: ZI_JIB_STATUS_CUBE plus seven supporting CDS views (ZI_JIB_DOC, ZI_JIB_DOC_AGG, ZI_JIB_YEAR_AGG, ZI_JIB_QTR_AGG, ZI_JIB_CLEARING, ZI_JIB_PERIOD, ZI_JIB_VENTURE)
Business requirement
Management dashboard card: for each joint venture, is the period's JIB posted and when was it entered - by month, quarter or fiscal year, with document drill-down (Fiori Custom Analytical Query).
Technical complexity

No venture on BKPF; JIB identified by document type from a GS01 set; reversals; months without a JIB must still show as Pending; entry date vs posting period; older S/4 release limits on CDS; delivery by abapGit ZIP to a system without ADT access.
Conventional approach
Analyse BKPF / BSEG / JV data in SE16N, design the views by trial activation, build and test each layer, rebuild on feedback - estimated 120 h (Very High new development).
How AI was used

Read the requirement workbook and production sample documents; designed the data model; wrote all eight views and the ZIP; rebuilt the model twice on client feedback (entry date model 04/11, posting period at document grain 06/11); added year / quarter aggregates, reversal handling, clearing data, navigation annotation and the all-ventures extension.
Human review and validation

Arnav confirmed the document-type set in GS03 and SE16N, imported and activated the views, worked with the GR consultant on the query, relayed two client test rounds, and fixed the launchpad navigation setting.
Result
Client (Corporate Accounts), 17/11/26: 'working well and meeting expectations'. 31 commits over 6 active days; 13 logged issues and changes handled; 1,110 lines of CDS.
Effort
120 h conventional vs 16 h with AI: 104 h (13 man-days) saved, 87% reduction.
Timeline
Requirement 03/11/26 -> first query running 04/11 -> client tests 06/11 -> navigation fixed 12/11 -> client confirmation 17/11 (11 working days, including four client additions).
Lessons
One object at a time with activation feedback; release constraints recorded once and reused; production samples checked line by line before the model is fixed; client test data drives the rebuild.

items: AI assistance is part of daily delivery, not a side experiment: 724 AI-assisted commits on 58 days, 70 use cases, three engagements in parallel.
The supportable effort reduction is 80% on the estimates, and still 60% if baselines are halved. 180 man-days of it are on work already confirmed in the system.

The gain comes from speed of first build and of root-cause analysis. It depends on human control: fresh source download before every change, activation feedback, functional confirmation, and a standing record of release constraints.

Next steps: (1) record activation / test results for the 32 tier-B items, which moves them to confirmed; (2) import the ATC batch and re-run ATC; (3) confirm the reporting project for the Astral engagement (T&G?); (4) log hours per object from now on, to replace estimates with actuals; (5) roll the toolkit (rules, memory, skills) out to the team.
